text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Turkish army defines its enemy as "fundamentalist activities" for the first time in history.
- A draft law on eight-year uninterrupted, compulsory education is ready to be presented for the cabinet's approval.
- The separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) cooperates with militant Islamists by training their hit squads in northern Iraq.
- Leftist leader Bulent Ecevit and main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz agree on a new government formula to replace the existing Islamist-led government.
- The Turkish army denies it is the governing power in Turkey in a briefing for reporters.
- Trade unions prepare for May Day celebrations throughout Turkey on Thursday.
- The British company Rolls Royce is to invest $7 million on energy in southeastern Mardin province.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan tells a meeting of his party he may call early elections.
